commentary.text: I’m taking an early central foothold with Red, occupying one of the four victory squares while keeping open lines for Yellow to reinforce the center.

I’m claiming a central square immediately while avoiding the exposed top-center sandwich: a Blue piece on (3,4) could be bracketed by Red next turn, whereas (4,4) is not presently vulnerable. This also keeps open a later push toward controlling the lower central pair.
```memo
### Position read
The opponent opened Red from (0,3) to central (3,3). We answered by moving Blue from (4,7) to (4,4), claiming a center square. Avoid (3,4) while Red remains at (3,3): Red could land at (3,5) and sandwich a piece there.
### Our plan
Contest the four center squares while checking same-color sandwich geometry before every placement. Seek the lower central pair, but respond to Yellow’s move rather than forcing Green into a tactically exposed square. Build same-color flanks for later captures.
### Opponent tendencies
Only one move observed: immediate central occupation with Red, suggesting a center-race strategy.
### Lessons
Teammates do not form capture pairs and can be friendly-fire victims. A piece moved into a sandwich is safe, but may be captured by a later enemy landing. Void pieces cannot capture but still count for center victory.
```
I’m claiming a second central square, building immediate center pressure while keeping Red and Yellow mutually supported as a team.

Green develops toward the open central square without entering Yellow’s immediate sandwich geometry. From (2,4), Green threatens to occupy (3,4) next cycle while preserving Blue’s hold on (4,4).
```memo
### Position read
The center is split: opponent pieces occupy (3,3) and (4,3), while we occupy (4,4); (3,4) remains empty. We developed Green from (2,0) to (2,4), directly above that open center square. No losses or eliminations.
### Our plan
If tactically safe and still open, move Green from (2,4) to (3,4), which would give us two central squares and deny an easy center sweep. Keep Blue at (4,4) unless moving it produces a concrete gain. Watch whether Red contests (3,4) or attacks the advanced Green.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has used both opening moves to occupy the left pair of central squares, strongly signaling a center-race strategy.
### Lessons
Before every central move, test possible same-color flanks. A teammate cannot complete a sandwich and may be captured within a mixed line. Moving into a sandwich is safe until a later capturing move triggers it.
```
I’m shifting Red across the center to occupy (3,4), denying Green that square while preserving Yellow’s potential horizontal capture of the Blue piece at (4,4).

I’m blocking Yellow’s immediate sandwich on our central Blue. Occupying (6,5) cuts the only clear route from (7,5) to (4,5), preserving our foothold at (4,4) while developing another Blue piece.
```memo
### Position read
The opponent holds (3,4) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; we hold (4,4) with Blue. Green remains at (2,4). Yellow threatened to move from (7,5) to (4,5), sandwiching our Blue at (4,4) against Yellow at (4,3). Blue moved (6,7) to (6,5), blocking that route. No losses or eliminations.
### Our plan
Preserve (4,4) and contest the remaining center square (3,3). On Green’s turn, consider moving Green from (3,0) to (3,3), but first check whether Red could immediately sandwich it by landing at (3,2) against Red at (3,4). Seek a safer way to undermine the two opposing center pieces; Green at (2,4) may become useful if Red leaves (3,4).
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is aggressively concentrating both colors in the center and created a direct sandwich threat against our central Blue.
### Lessons
Trace every same-color landing-and-flank capture before moving. Movement blockers can defend a sandwich target by denying the attacker access to the required landing square.
```
I’m tightening the net around the Blue piece in the center. This move blocks its downward exit, leaving only the right side open while preserving our Red–Yellow hold on two central squares.

I’m contesting the last open central square immediately. Green may be vulnerable to a Red sandwich from (3,2), but this forces the opponent to spend a move removing it and prevents an uncontested three-piece center formation.
```memo
### Position read
We now occupy center squares (3,3) with Green and (4,4) with Blue; the opponent occupies (3,4) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow. Yellow moved from (7,4) to (5,4). No losses yet. Green at (3,3) can be sandwiched if Red lands at (3,2), using Red at (3,4) as the far flank; Red at (0,2) currently has a clear route there.
### Our plan
Keep contesting the center and preserve Blue at (4,4). If Red spends its turn capturing Green at (3,3), use Blue’s reply to improve central defense or create a counter-threat. Continue blocking Yellow’s route to (4,5); Blue at (6,5) currently blocks the original Yellow piece on (7,5).
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is concentrating both colors centrally and looks for same-color sandwich geometry against our central Blue.
### Lessons
Immediate center occupation can force tempo even when the occupying piece is tactically vulnerable. Recheck landing squares that enable same-color flanks, especially (3,2) against Green at (3,3).
```
I’m exploiting the Red anchor on (3,4): landing at (3,2) sandwiches the central Green piece on (3,3), removing it and opening a center square for Team A to claim later.

I’m developing a safe route back into the center. Blue moves across the open first row, preparing to occupy (3,3) on a later turn while avoiding the immediate Red sandwich geometry around row 3.
```memo
### Position read
The opponent used Red at (3,2) with Red at (3,4) to capture our Green on (3,3); our Green loss count is now 1. The center remains split: opponent pieces occupy (3,4) and (4,3), while our Blue occupies (4,4); (3,3) is empty. Blue has moved from (1,7) to (1,3), with a clear vertical route toward (3,3) unless the opponent blocks it.

### Our plan
Reoccupy (3,3) with Blue when tactically safe, which would give us three central squares if the opponent’s two occupants can be displaced. Preserve Blue at (4,4), and watch for a Yellow sandwich using Yellow at (4,3). Green should support the center without entering the same Red flank between (3,2) and (3,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent actively recognizes same-color sandwich geometry and immediately punished our vulnerable central Green. Both opponent colors remain concentrated near the center.

### Lessons
Before entering a gap, check for stationary same-color enemy flanks on both sides. Develop pieces along clear files so central occupation can be restored without exposing them immediately.
```
I’m bringing the outer Yellow piece onto row 4 to establish a same-color flank against Blue’s central piece and strengthen our center-pressure options.

The open sixth row lets Green complete a long vertical sandwich against Green at (2,4). This removes two central opponent pieces at the acceptable cost of one Blue piece, breaking their center control and equalizing Green’s earlier loss.
```memo
### Position read
Green’s move from (6,0) to (6,4) creates a vertical sandwich with Green at (2,4), capturing Yellow (5,4), our Blue (4,4), and Red (3,4). Expected losses become Red 1, Blue 1, Yellow 1, Green 1. After removal, only the opponent’s Yellow at (4,3) occupies the center; (3,3), (3,4), and (4,4) are empty. Our Blue at (1,3) retains a clear route toward (3,3).

### Our plan
Use Blue’s coming turn to rebuild center presence, especially via (3,3), while checking immediate Red threats. Green at (2,4) and the newly advanced Green at (6,4) provide useful vertical influence, but avoid another sandwich that burns teammates without sufficient return.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent develops aggressively around the center and notices same-color sandwich geometry. Yellow recently placed at (4,6), creating a potential horizontal sandwich against pieces between it and Yellow at (4,3).

### Lessons
Mixed-color sandwich lines can justify friendly fire when they remove multiple opponent pieces and decisively reset center control. Always scan long files between two same-color pieces, not just adjacent formations.
```
I’m advancing Red into the center, joining Yellow’s foothold and setting up a potential horizontal sandwich if Blue contests the adjacent central square.

Blue takes (3,4) to block the opponent’s developing center majority. The piece is safe from an immediate sandwich, and occupying the fourth central lane prevents Yellow from completing a rapid center takeover.
```memo
### Position read
Blue moved from (3,7) to center square (3,4), blocking the opponent’s center threat. The opponent currently holds (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; we hold (3,4), while (4,4) is empty. Green pieces at (2,4) and (6,4) influence the remaining center square, though neither can reach it while intervening occupancy blocks the file.

### Our plan
Contest (4,4) and prevent the opponent from controlling all four central squares. On Green’s next turn, reassess whether (6,4) can advance toward the center or whether a tactical wall/capture is available after Yellow moves. Preserve Blue at (3,4) unless a favorable sandwich emerges.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is prioritizing central occupation and has coordinated Red and Yellow on the left half of the center. Expect Yellow to consider (4,4) from (4,6).

### Lessons
When the opponent already holds adjacent center squares, occupying the remaining accessible center square can be more urgent than speculative captures. Recheck center victory after every move.
```
I’m consolidating our hold on the center and setting up Red’s next-turn sandwich against the Blue piece on (3,4).

Green shifts laterally to (2,5), blocking Red’s open route from (0,5) to (3,5), which would otherwise sandwich and capture our Blue center piece. This preserves our foothold at (3,4) and keeps the opponent from consolidating the center.
```memo
### Position read
The opponent occupies (3,3), (4,3), and (4,4); we occupy (3,4). Red threatened (0,5)→(3,5), which would sandwich our Blue at (3,4) against Red at (3,3). Green moved (2,4)→(2,5) to block that file. Losses are 1 for every color; no eliminations.

### Our plan
Hold Blue at (3,4) because it prevents immediate center victory. Use Green to obstruct flanking routes and seek a way to dislodge the adjacent Yellow pair. Reassess all captures and center occupation after Red’s move; develop Green from (6,4) if a route toward (4,4) opens.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is strongly prioritizing the four central squares and may try to remove our lone central blocker through a same-color sandwich.

### Lessons
Check whether an opponent can land beyond a central blocker and sandwich it against a same-colored piece. A quiet line-blocking move can be essential defense.
```
I’m developing a same-color Red flank along row 3. From (3,6), Red threatens to close toward the central Blue piece while maintaining our three-square grip on the center.

I’m exploiting the central alignment: Blue lands at (5,4), sandwiching Yellow at (4,4) against our Blue piece at (3,4). This weakens the opponent’s center grip and brings Yellow to two losses; Green can then occupy (3,5) to block Red’s new horizontal capture threat.
```memo
### Position read
Blue moved (5,7)→(5,4), sandwiching Yellow at (4,4) against Blue at (3,4). Yellow now has 2 losses; all other colors have 1. The center is occupied by opponent pieces at (3,3) and (4,3), with our Blue at (3,4). Red at (3,6) threatens (3,6)→(3,5), which would sandwich Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3).

### Our plan
On Green’s next turn, strongly prefer (2,5)→(3,5) if legal, occupying Red’s required landing square and preserving our central Blue blocker. Continue targeting Yellow’s remaining central piece at (4,3); one more Yellow capture eliminates that color. Watch for any immediate center-occupation threat after Yellow moves.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes the center and has repeatedly created same-color flanking threats against our lone central blocker. Expect Yellow to interfere with the planned Green block or build protection around (4,3).

### Lessons
Exploit sandwiches where an existing central piece supplies the far flank. After every capture, check whether the moved piece or central blocker remains vulnerable before the opponent’s next same-color turn.
```
I’m bringing a reserve Yellow piece toward the center, supporting the Yellow piece already on (4,3) and preparing to occupy the remaining central squares after Red addresses the Blue piece on (3,4).

I’m occupying (3,5) to deny Red the landing square it needs to sandwich our Blue center piece. This preserves our central foothold while we prepare to capture Yellow’s remaining central piece.
```memo
### Position read
Green moved (2,5)→(3,5), blocking Red’s threatened (3,6)→(3,5) sandwich of our Blue at (3,4). The center holds opponent pieces at (3,3) and (4,3), plus our Blue at (3,4); (4,4) is empty. Yellow has 2 losses, while every other color has 1.

### Our plan
Preserve the Blue center blocker and seek one capture of Yellow to eliminate that color. Yellow’s key pieces are at (4,2) and (4,3), with the latter central. On Blue’s next turn, first check for a direct sandwich or enclosure against either. Also watch whether Red can remove Green at (3,5) and renew the horizontal threat.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central occupation and attacks our central blocker using same-color flanks. Yellow’s last move reinforced the row-4 cluster instead of immediately filling the last center square.

### Lessons
A safe blocker can be more valuable than a speculative capture. Recheck all four center squares after every move, and remember mixed-color adjacent lines can be captured only when bounded by the moving color.
```
I’m advancing Red directly above Blue’s central piece, restricting its vertical mobility while building pressure around the center without disturbing our two occupied central squares.

I’m reinforcing the center with a second Blue piece. This denies easy central progress, keeps our key blocker supported, and creates a stronger base for attacking Yellow, which is one capture from elimination.
```memo
### Position read
Blue moved (5,4)→(4,4). We now occupy both right-hand center squares, while the opponent occupies (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow. Yellow remains at 2 losses; all other colors have 1. Red pieces at (3,3) and (3,6) bracket our Blue (3,4) and Green (3,5), but no capture occurs without a new Red landing move.

### Our plan
Keep at least one Blue center blocker secure and seek one capture of Yellow to eliminate it. The vulnerable Yellow center pair is at (4,2)-(4,3); establishing a Blue flank on row 4 could sandwich both against Blue at (4,4). On Green’s next turn, check for captures first, then reinforce or obstruct routes toward our center pieces.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is concentrating around the center and constructing same-color flanks for multi-piece captures. Red’s latest move to (2,4) may support a future vertical attack, so watch column 4 carefully.

### Lessons
Captures only trigger from the landing piece, so static brackets are dormant threats. Preserve center occupation while checking every move for mixed-color sandwich lines and enclosure.
```

I’m advancing the spare Yellow piece onto row 5, creating a direct threat to slide to (5,5) and sandwich Blue’s piece at (6,5) against Yellow at (7,5). This also preserves our central occupation at (4,3).

I’m repositioning Red onto the open fifth row, creating an immediate threat to land at (5,4) and sandwich both central Blue pieces against the Red piece at (2,4). This forces Blue to disrupt the formation while preserving Red’s central presence.

I’m advancing Blue into (2,3), creating a direct next-turn sandwich threat against the Red piece on (2,4) with Blue’s piece on the right edge. This pressures Red to abandon or defend that useful central post while Blue keeps both occupied center squares intact.
```memo
### Position read
We hold Blue on both right-center squares (3,4) and (4,4). The opponent holds Red (3,3) and Yellow (4,3); Yellow has 2 losses, while every other color has 1. Blue has advanced to (2,3), threatening to move the edge Blue from (2,7) to (2,5) and sandwich Red at (2,4).

### Our plan
Preserve our two center squares and exploit Yellow’s one-capture elimination threshold. If Red vacates (2,4), use the gained tempo to improve Blue’s flank. On Green’s next turn, make a legal move without fail; Green’s previous turn was a pass, so another consecutive pass would eliminate and remove Green.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent concentrates pieces around the center and disrupts prepared same-color brackets before they can trigger.

### Lessons
Only a landing move triggers capture. Check unobstructed rook paths, matching-color far endpoints, the acting color, and pending consecutive-pass danger every turn.
```
I’m using the Yellow pair on column 5 to sandwich Blue at (6,5), putting Blue one loss from elimination while advancing Yellow toward the center.

I’m keeping Green on (3,5) to deny Red the landing that would eliminate Blue at (3,4). This move establishes a Green endpoint on column 3, threatening a future sweep from below through Yellow, Red, and Blue; it should force the opponent to break the line while Blue prepares to escape Yellow’s bracket at (4,4).
```memo
### Position read
Blue has 2 losses and must avoid one more capture. Green remains at (3,5), preventing Red from landing there and sandwiching Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3). Yellow can next capture Blue (4,4) by moving (5,5) to (4,5), unless Blue moves or disrupts this on its intervening turn. Yellow also has 2 losses.

### Our plan
We moved Green to (1,3), creating a latent column-3 sweep: Green could later land at (5,3) and bracket Yellow (4,3), Red (3,3), and Blue (2,3) against Green (1,3). This would eliminate Yellow but also Blue, so use it only if the trade is favorable; primarily it pressures the opponent to vacate or break the line. On Blue’s next turn, save Blue (4,4) from Yellow’s immediate bracket while preserving center prospects.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent concentrates around the center, attacks Blue’s one-capture elimination threshold, and breaks visible same-color brackets.

### Lessons
Keep Green (3,5) occupied while Red (3,3) and Blue (3,4) remain aligned. Before every move, check whether either vulnerable Blue can be sandwiched on the next opponent turn.
```
I’m exploiting the Red anchor on (3,3): landing on (3,6) sandwiches Green and Blue along row 3. This eliminates Blue immediately and leaves Green one loss from elimination.

I’m keeping our Void piece on (4,4) as a center blocker and advancing the remote Blue piece to (4,7), where it can later reinforce the fourth rank without disturbing Green’s latent column-three tactic.
```memo
### Position read
Blue is eliminated; its Void pieces cannot capture but remain useful blockers. The opponent occupies center squares (3,3) and (4,3), while Blue safely blocks (4,4). Green has 2 losses, so any further Green capture eliminates it. Current Green pieces do not appear immediately sandwichable by Yellow.

### Our plan
We moved the remote Blue Void from (2,7) to (4,7), preserving Blue (4,4) as the critical center blocker and preparing lateral reinforcement along row 4. Keep Green alive while seeking tactical captures against Yellow, which has 2 losses. Green (1,3) still creates a latent sweep by landing at (5,3) through Blue (2,3), Red (3,3), and Yellow (4,3), but this would remove Blue too and should be used only when strategically worthwhile.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is concentrating near the center and deliberately targeting pieces whose colors are one loss from elimination.

### Lessons
Void Blue should prioritize blocking center squares and obstructing lanes. Before each Green move, check every possible opponent sandwich because one captured Green causes elimination.
```

I’m creating a vertical Yellow sandwich threat against the Green piece on (6,4): next Yellow turn, (5,5) can move to (5,4), using this piece as the far flank. This should force Green to retreat while preserving Red’s route to the upper center.

I’m removing Green from the immediate Red–Blue–Green sandwich on column 3. The move keeps our remaining active color alive through Red’s turn and preserves the central Blue blocker.
```memo
### Position read
Blue is eliminated. Green has 2 losses, so one capture ends the game. We moved Green from (1,3) to (0,3), preventing Red from landing at (0,3) and sandwiching it through Void Blue (2,3) against Red (3,3). A severe threat remains: Yellow can move (5,5) to (5,4), sandwiching Green (6,4) against Yellow (7,4).

### Our plan
If Green survives, immediately reassess all one-move sandwiches before pursuing captures. Preserve Void Blue (4,4) as the central blocker. Yellow has 2 losses, so capturing any Yellow eliminates that color and may neutralize its capture threats.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent concentrates around the center and actively targets colors one loss from elimination.

### Lessons
With both colors at or beyond the elimination threshold, every turn is tactical survival. Check sandwiches using mixed-color lines, including Void pieces, and prioritize removing the opponent’s landing squares or far flanks.
```
I close the gap on the top edge, sandwiching Green at (0,3) between two Red pieces. This third Green loss eliminates Green; with Blue already eliminated, Team A wins immediately.

I’m using our Void Blue piece to occupy (5,4), removing Yellow’s landing square for the immediate sandwich of Green at (6,4). This keeps Green alive for its next turn.
```memo
### Position read
Blue is eliminated and Green has 2 losses. Void Blue moved from (4,4) to (5,4), blocking Yellow’s threatened move from (5,5) to (5,4), which would have sandwiched Green (6,4) against Yellow (7,4). The center now contains opponent pieces at (3,3) and (4,3), while (3,4) and (4,4) are empty.

### Our plan
On Green’s next turn, first check every immediate sandwich and enclosure threat because one Green capture loses the game. Seek a safe capture of Yellow: Yellow has 2 losses, so one capture eliminates it. Keep Green (6,4) protected by denying useful Yellow landing squares or moving it if necessary.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent concentrates near the center and targets colors one loss from elimination. Expect Yellow to create another tactical threat rather than make a slow positional move.

### Lessons
Void pieces cannot capture but remain valuable blockers and mobile shields. When one loss means defeat, occupying an enemy capture landing square can be stronger than preserving center control.
```

Yellow closes the vertical sandwich against the Yellow piece on (7,4), capturing the Blue Void and Green pieces below. Green’s third loss eliminates Green, so with Blue already eliminated, Team A wins immediately.
